chapter: Chicago years: recordings, Armstrong, wartime exit
title: Sitting in with Bob Crosby's band
summary: He saw no famous Chicago sessions except Bob Crosby's. Crosby's crew chartered his excursion boat, then he and Oliver Alcorn jammed with them, his only time with Crosby.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Herb, were you ever present at any of those famous Chicago recording sessions like the Hot Fives or any of the Oliver sessions? No.

The only one I was present at was Bob Crossby. They had a recording session before us. We came on after them, and them fellas was really small guys. They had a case of scotch and soda, and they had heard a whole lot of talk of the Harlem Ham Fats, so they invited us in the studio, and we drank, listened at them recording. And after they finished, we started recording, and they stood a while and heard us a while. Now, getting back to the Navy Pinnah, Bob Crossby and his full crew chartered the boat that I used to play on, Steamship North Show. I said make trips for half an hour on the lake, so they chartered the boat that night. So after they came on, well, it was off that night, so Bob Crossby came to me and asked me what I care to sit in, and at that time they called it Jam with the Boys, since we were from New Orleans. So me and Oliver Alcorn, tennis sax man, he picked us two out. He didn't take the rest of the boys. So we really had a real New Orleans session. I can't describe it. They took pictures, moving pictures, and I've never had a chance to see one of them. Somebody's got them somewhere. I'd sure like to see one of them. And we really had a session. Bob Zerke, the piano, he's dead now. Miller, for Zola, he's dead too. And had a young trumpet player, I think that made all the famous recordings. He had two trumpets. And we started slinging some real New Orleans stuff. And I really enjoyed Bob Crossby asking me to sit in with such a great band. And I don't think you'll go nowhere in New Orleans or anywhere and find a better jazz band than Bob Crossby, the original.
Well, tell me, did you play with Crossby at any other time, any later date? No, no.
That was the only time with Crossby.
